The biggest local step is the Village transfer stamp, which every Hanover Park seller has to buy before closing. The second is working out which county records your deed, since the village straddles Cook and DuPage counties. Everything else follows the usual path of listing, selling on your own, or accepting an as-is cash offer.

  • Listing with an agent: the most exposure, with showings and buyer repair requests.
  • Selling on your own: you manage the marketing and the paperwork, often with an attorney reviewing the contract.
  • As-is cash purchase: fewer contingencies and a closing date you can usually choose, with the buyer accepting the house's condition.

Start the stamp request early, because the Village needs notice and every balance owed to it has to be settled first.

If you are unsure whether anything is owed, ask Finance for a balance check before you accept an offer. A forgotten parking ticket or code invoice is the most common reason a stamp is held up.

Delays in Hanover Park usually come from the Village side of the sale, so work through it in order.

  1. Check your tax bill or title commitment for the county and the parcel number.
  2. Pay anything owed to the Village, including tickets, invoices, liens, judgments and the water balance, and ask Water Billing for the closing read.
  3. Fill out the MyDec or PTAX-203 form and the Village's Real Estate Transfer Tax Declaration form, and attach the deed.
  4. Call Finance at least three business days before closing, or email the set, and ask for the current stamp rate.
  5. Hand the stamp to your title company so the deed can be recorded with the right county office.

An as-is cash buyer removes the lender's appraisal and repair requests from the timeline, but the stamp, the water account and the county filing are still required. If the house is a rental, ask Code Enforcement about the license and any open violations at the same time, so nothing owed to the Village surfaces on closing week.

All residents selling a home in Hanover Park must buy a Transfer Tax Stamp from the Village before the closing. The homeowner, realtor or lawyer calls the Finance Department at 630-823-5790 at least three business days before closing, and walk-in requests are not honored.

  • Have the MyDec or PTAX-203 form ready.
  • Complete the Village of Hanover Park Real Estate Transfer Tax Declaration form.
  • Include the deed, and email the set to financedepartment@hpil.org if you prefer.
  • Pay everything owed to the Village first: tickets, invoices, liens, judgments and the final water bill.

A quitclaim deed also needs a stamp. In that case the Village asks for a copy of the signed, notarized deed plus its own declaration form. Ask Finance for the current stamp rate, since the amount depends on the value of the sale.

Do not wait for the last week. If the balance is clear and the reading is booked, the Finance Department can issue the stamp on the day you call, and your title company will not be chasing the Village for paperwork at the closing table.

Water bills go out on the first of each month and are due by the 21st, whatever day of the week that falls on. A payment that is not received by then draws a 10 percent penalty, and a termination notice is mailed on the 22nd.

Because an unpaid final water bill blocks the transfer stamp, arrange the closing read with Water Billing early. You can email waterbilling@hpil.org with your property address in the subject line, and a representative replies with forms or instructions, so there is no need for a trip to Village Hall. Log in to your water account on the Village website to check the balance before you call.

Hanover Park lies in both Cook and DuPage counties, so the recorder depends on where your parcel is. Your tax bill or title commitment shows the county and the parcel number.

For Cook County parcels, the Cook County Clerk's recordings office requires the preparer's and mail-to names and addresses, the common address, the Property Index Number and a legal description. A deed also needs grantor and grantee names and addresses, a completed MyDec declaration and any municipal transfer tax, which in Hanover Park is the stamp described above. An exemption statement is added where one applies.

For DuPage parcels, the DuPage County Recorder asks for a completed deed, the PTAX form or an exemption statement, municipal transfer stamps if applicable, the grantee's name and address for tax bills, the permanent parcel number, the legal description and the preparer's name and address. The DuPage office accepts PTAX-203 forms completed in MyDec and supports eRecording through several vendors. Title companies usually take care of these filings.

Hanover Park is a dense suburb of about 6.5 square miles with 36,568 residents and large households. About 91.5 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which points to long tenure in many homes. Many sellers speak a language other than English at home, so plain-language or translated paperwork helps.

Of the 11,732 housing units counted in 2020, 2.8 percent were vacant. Metra's Hanover Park station on the Milwaukee District West Line is in fare zone 4, and Pace Route 554 reaches Elgin and Schaumburg.

Several districts overlap here, and six different public high schools serve the village. Elgin Area School District U-46 is the largest, covering about 90 square miles across Cook, DuPage and Kane counties.

  • Schaumburg Township Elementary District 54
  • Township High School District 211
  • Community Consolidated School District 93
  • Glenbard Township High School District 87
  • Keeneyville School District 20
  • Lake Park High School District 108

Your address determines the district, and buyers who have children check this first. Library service comes from the Poplar Creek Public Library District or the Schaumburg Township District Library depending on the part of town.

The Village licenses all residential rental properties, and the Code Enforcement Unit inspects them. An owner needs to pass an inspection and attend a landlord training seminar before getting a rental license. The Crime Free Multi-Housing Program requires landlords to attend training and use a crime free lease addendum.

If you are selling a rented house, ask Code Enforcement at 630-823-5570 about the license and any open violations before you list. You can report a problem on the 24 hour hotline at 630-823-5572, and an officer usually investigates within 24 to 48 hours. Building permits for work on the property come from the Community Development Department, not Code Enforcement.

faqs.q: Do I have to buy a transfer stamp to sell my Hanover Park house?
faqs.a: Yes. The Village requires all home sellers to buy a Transfer Tax Stamp before closing. Call Finance at 630-823-5790 at least three business days ahead.

faqs.q: What blocks the stamp in Hanover Park?
faqs.a: Unpaid money owed to the Village. Tickets, invoices, liens, judgments and the final water bill must all be paid before the stamp is issued.

faqs.q: Does a quitclaim deed need the stamp?
faqs.a: Yes. A quitclaim deed requires a stamp, and the Village asks for a copy of the signed, notarized deed with its transfer tax declaration form.

faqs.q: Which county records my Hanover Park deed?
faqs.a: Cook County or DuPage County, depending on where the parcel sits. The village spans both, so check your tax bill or title paperwork.

faqs.q: When are Hanover Park water bills due?
faqs.a: On or before the 21st of each month. A balance unpaid by then gets a 10 percent penalty, so clear it before you request the transfer stamp.
